Server asks for a user name and password before webtrees (directory protection)?

Only if your web server protects the whole site with its own user name and password (the browser shows a small sign-in box before webtrees opens, e.g. .htaccess). Enter those here; the webtrees sign-in follows separately.

The server asks for its own sign-in before webtrees (e.g. SSO, OAuth or web server password protection). If it is a password protection of the web server (the browser shows a small sign-in box), enter that user name and password under “directory protection” on this screen. With an SSO service the operator has to let the app’s requests bypass that sign-in; the webtrees login itself still applies.
The web server rejected the user name or password of the directory protection. Check both under “directory protection” on this screen.

You find the address in your browser: open your family site and copy the address at the top – the app trims the rest.
Address taken from the clipboard – check it and click “Connect”.

Easiest: in webtrees, open the “App” menu and click “Connect with %1$s” – %1$s then takes care of everything, there is nothing to type here. By hand: click “Copy address” there, %1$s fills the address in here; then sign in with your webtrees username and password.
Even easier: in webtrees, open the “App” menu and tap “Connect now” – then there is nothing to type here.

Server: %1$s
Account: %2$s
Family tree: %3$s

%1$s %2$s – a client for webtrees. With your own webtrees server it needs the api4webtrees module there.
This list needs the whole tree at once – the server must run api4webtrees 1.9 or later.
All surnames with count, period and the most frequent places.
All places – only with counts, with the surnames found there, or with the individuals and their events.
All marriages with date and number of children, alphabetical or chronological.
Who had which occupation or religion.
All baptisms with their godparents in chronological order.
As anniversary calendar (by month and day)
The family book needs the whole tree at once – the server must run api4webtrees 1.9 or later.

All families of the tree like a local family book: spouses with a reference to their parents’ family, marriage, children with a reference to their own family. With a place, only the families of that place.
Farms and houses from the place manager: places with a type (farm, house …) in their location record below the place. Each with its history, residents and owners; families point to their house.
Only houses and farms (by place type)

Houses and farms only, judged by the location record’s type (house, farm, mill, church …); parts of town, villages and districts are chapter headings. Without a type, a house number in the name counts.
Places with neither a type nor a house number go into the house section too; otherwise they go into the appendix.
All descendants of the root person generation by generation, with spouses, children and cross-references, numbered as you choose, with indexes.
Branch colours (one per child of the progenitors)
Table of contents: click and press F9 (LibreOffice: Tools → Update → Indexes).
All ancestors of the root person with vital data, baptisms, burials, sources and notes, by generation and Kekulé number, with indexes.
Descendant and family books will follow.
%1$d earliest known ancestors – ancestors whose parents are unknown.
All ancestors by generation with Kekulé numbers; anyone appearing twice refers to their first number.
The ancestors where research ends, by the four grandparent lines.
The male line generation by generation, with the wives.
The female line generation by generation, with the husbands.
How complete each generation is – as a table, with pedigree collapse.
All descendants with numbers, spouses and marriages.
How many descendants there are in each generation – men, women, living, name bearers.
Births and deaths of all visible persons in chronological order.
All details of the root person on one page.
… and %1$d more pages in the PDF
Opens in the browser – you may need to sign in there.
No bookmarks yet. Right-click a person and choose “Bookmark”.
All descendants of a person on one sheet, the starting person at the top, one row per generation.
Save sheets as PDF (with assembly plan)
The mouse wheel zooms around the pointer, dragging moves, a click switches between the whole sheet and reading size. Right-click a box to colour its branch.
All ancestors of a person on one sheet, the starting person at the bottom, each generation one row above.
The paternal and maternal grandparents with all their descendants: uncles, aunts and cousins. Father and mother stand side by side in the middle, the starting person and siblings below them.
Ancestors above and descendants below the starting person, on one sheet.
The ancestors of both partners side by side, the couple in the middle, their common descendants below. Kekulé numbers count from 1 for each partner.
The first matching rule colours the box. The rules apply to all charts of this tree.
Right-click a box in the preview to colour the person together with their ancestors or descendants on the chart.
Final size %1$d × %2$d cm · %3$d strips of %4$s m
Assembly plan: %1$d A4 sheets (%2$d columns × %3$d rows), final size %4$d × %5$d cm
Lay out the sheets by their labels (A1 top left). Each sheet overlaps its neighbour by 1 cm – trim at the crop marks and glue.

The descendants on A4 pages of a few generations each. Below each person of the bottom row it says on which page their descendants continue; a page overview in front and an index of persons with page numbers at the back – for a binder or a book.

The descendants of all root couples of one ancestor generation side by side, the paternal side on the left – all blood relatives on one sheet. Anyone appearing more than once is shown in full once; elsewhere a box refers to the grid position.
Loading person data for the cards …
pedigree collapse: ancestors under this number
other position of the same person (grid)
Note where the chart ends (+3 children)
Chart as fold-out page (A3, PDF only)
The ancestors as life bars on a time axis – who lived when, who at the same time. Oldest generation at the top; unknown ends estimated (dashed), optionally with historical events.

1618|1648|Thirty Years’ War;1683|1699|Great Turkish War;1756|1763|Seven Years’ War;1806|1815|Napoleonic Wars;1816|1817|Year without a summer;1845|1855|Emigration wave;1848|1849|Revolutions of 1848;1861|1865|American Civil War;1870|1871|Franco-Prussian War;1880|1893|Emigration wave;1914|1918|First World War;1918|1920|Spanish flu;1929|1933|Great Depression;1939|1945|Second World War;1945|1950|Flight and expulsion;1961|1989|Berlin Wall

How are two people related? At the top the nearest common ancestor (or couple), below the two lines down to the people; the relationship is shown below the title. Generations = how far back to search.
Four generations per A4 page in landscape. Above each person of the top row it says on which page their ancestors continue – for a binder or a book.
The male line: father, his father and so on, one generation per row.
The female line: mother, her mother and so on, one generation per row.
The line from the starting person to the ancestor with the earliest known birth.
Grid at the margin (columns and generations)
Connect duplicate persons with a line
The root person in the middle, each generation of ancestors a ring around them, as a half circle.
Like the fan chart, as a full circle.
All rules and limits as default

Checks the whole tree as far as you may see it. Errors are contradictions in the data; warnings are unusual but possible. Click shows the person, double-click opens the person sheet, the pencil edits the event, the tick marks a finding as checked – it comes back only if the data change.
Estimate missing birth and death from baptism and burial
New family tree on this PC

Start from scratch or switch from another program: %1$s keeps your family tree on this computer. No server, no password, no internet needed. If the family should see it later, the tree moves with its photos to a NAS or web host via GEDCOM export – you keep using the program as before.
Switching from another program: export there as GEDCOM (.ged) and import it here – people, families, sources and notes. The file itself stays unchanged.
The family tree could not be created. Please report this at github.com/thobgg/app4webtrees/issues and attach the file %1$s. The details below help to find the cause.
Family tree on this PC: includes webtrees %1$s (webtrees.net, GPL-3), unchanged from the official release.
Family tree on this PC: not available, missing %1$s
%1$s is not an official webtrees product. Questions and bug reports please at github.com/thobgg/app4webtrees/issues.
Behind the scenes this is webtrees: everything the webtrees website can do is available via “Open webtrees in the browser”.
Kekulé numbers: the central person is 1, the father twice the number, the mother twice plus 1. Men even, women odd.
Kekulé counts ancestors (father 2, mother 3 …). Chronicle gives generation and running number (IV-12). d’Aboville counts descendants (1.2.3 = third child of the second child).
1.2.3: the child’s number per generation, with dots. d’Aboville: the same with the root couple’s letter in front (C1.2.3). Henry: without dots (123). Serial: 1, 2, 3 in reading order.
Only the children of sons, i.e. the descendants who carry the central person’s surname.
Show the married-in parent in each generation too, not only the line itself.
Persons without a death date with names only, no birth or places – for sharing with others.
Leave out unmarried and childless descendants; the chart stays smaller.
Hide children who died before the chosen age; the chart stays clear.
Where the chart ends, a small hint such as “+3 children” or “↑ more ancestors”.
One page per person with all details behind the chart. In the PDF, a click on the box jumps there and back.
If the birth is missing, the baptism is shown instead; if the death is missing, the burial – with its own symbol in the legend.
The call name marked in webtrees is underlined, as usual in genealogy.
Generations as columns from left to right instead of rows – good for wide prints and screens.
Letters and numbers at the margin like on a map; references to duplicate persons name the position (B3).
All persons alphabetically with their position on the chart, on a page of its own.
If a person appears more than once on the chart, a curved line connects the positions.
Explains the symbols (* † ⚭), the numbers, the colours and the colour rules at the bottom of the chart.
Wars, famine years and eras as bars above the timeline, to place the dates in context.
A first page shows which person is on which page.
How many generations fit on one A4 page; the continuation appears as “→ p. 7” below the person.
From which ancestral generation the descendants are shown: parents (siblings), grandparents (cousins), great-grandparents (second cousins) …
How many generations below the central person are added: children, grandchildren …
Siblings of the central person or of all ancestors on the chart; “of all ancestors” makes it much wider.
Ancestor chart upside down: the central person on top, the ancestors below.
Sex: blue and red. Grandparent line: the central person’s four lines in four colours. Branch: one colour per child of the root couple.
Original size prints as large as the chart is calculated. Width in cm scales it. On sheets spreads the chart over A4 pages for gluing, with an assembly plan.
Roll width of the plotter or copy shop; the PDF page gets exactly this width.
Shrink the chart so that it fits the roll in one strip; otherwise several strips are produced.
Save all settings of this chart as a file (.wtvorlage) – for later or for another person.
Load a saved template; it replaces the current settings.
Sorted by month and day instead of year – for anniversaries and the family newsletter.
Full dates (12 March 1851) instead of the year only.
Only the place name without district and country, e.g. “Winterbach” instead of “Winterbach, Rems-Murr-Kreis, Württemberg”. A short name set in the place manager takes precedence.
Ancestors who appear via several lines (pedigree collapse) written out in full each time instead of “see no.”.
The matching chart as an A3 page at the back of the book, to fold out; PDF only.
Colour mark at the page margin: in the ancestor book the four grandparent lines, in the descendant book one colour per child of the root couple.
Strict reports more, generous less; the rules’ limits change with it. Own values turn it into “Own settings”.
If the birth is missing, the baptism counts as birth; if the death is missing, the burial. So the age rules work with pure parish register data too.
From this value on the rule reports; the default is shown on the right.
Errors are contradictions in the data, warnings are only unusual. Changeable per rule.
Save the tick list as a file – for a second computer or a fellow researcher.
Load a saved tick list; it is merged into the existing one.
Click a column header to sort, click again to reverse. Double-click or Enter: show the person as focus. Right-click: more commands.

Type into the fields below the column headers: text finds parts ("hann" finds Hannover). 1800-1850 under birth or death: years from–to. ! = field empty, * = field filled. Baptism is shown with ~ when the birth is missing, burial with □ when the death is missing.
This event exists more than once. The form edits the first one; the others stay unchanged and are shown in “Full” mode.
Not recognised as a date – saved as date text
Not everything was saved – your input is still there, please save again.
Simple: one form with name, birth, baptism, religion, occupation, marriage, death and burial. Full: all events as a table.

Select an event in the table to see its notes and sources.
Select a source on the left.
How reliable the evidence is: primary source (photo or original of the entry), secondary source (transcript), questionable, unreliable or estimated.
Transcript of the entry – makes the text searchable later
Source, page, quality, date, quotation and note are copied. For relatives and partnerships the citation is attached to the record, not to an event.
Remove the citation of “%1$s” from this event? The source itself is kept.
Publisher, place, year – or the web address for online sources
Delete the source “%1$s”? It is cited by %2$d individuals or families; these citations will be lost too.
Delete the source “%1$s”? Nobody cites it.
%1$d sources are not cited by anyone. Untick what should stay.
Creates a source from a scan or photo (certificate, parish register page, newspaper notice): title from the file name, the file attached as a document. It is then selected and can be cited.
How well the tree is sourced: individuals and events with a source, photos, per event type – and who has no source at all yet.
The file stays in the archive. A media object is only created by your choice – for files that do not have one yet.
Not a valid date – please check (e.g. 12 Mar 1850, March 1850, about 1850, before 1850, between 1850 and 1852)

These individuals are probably duplicates: same name and one identical event date (rule 219) or a similar name with a close year of birth (228). “Merge …” shows both side by side and you choose what stays. Every merge is logged and can be undone as long as nobody has edited the records since.
For duplicates the rules do not find, such as children with the same name and no data. The first individual stays, the second is absorbed into it.
Preselected: everything of the first individual, from the second only what the first does not have word for word. Links to families and media always stay.
